text: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his steadfast love endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods; his steadfast love endures forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who alone does great wonders; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who made the heavens with understanding; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who spread out the earth upon the waters; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who made the great lights; his steadfast love endures forever.
The sun to rule over the day; his steadfast love endures forever.
The moon and stars to rule over the night; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who struck down Egypt's firstborn; his steadfast love endures forever.
And brought Israel out from among them; his steadfast love endures forever.
With a strong hand and an outstretched arm; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who split the Red Sea in two; his steadfast love endures forever. [footnote: Hebrew: Sea of Reeds]

versions.text: To him who split the Red Sea in two; his steadfast love endures forever.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote clarifying that the Hebrew reads "Sea of Reeds" would help readers, since the same term appears again in verse 15.

text: And led Israel through the midst of it; his steadfast love endures forever.
But swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who led his people through the wilderness; his steadfast love endures forever.
To him who struck down great kings; his steadfast love endures forever.
And killed mighty kings; his steadfast love endures forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites; his steadfast love endures forever.
And Og, king of Bashan; his steadfast love endures forever.
And gave their land as an inheritance; his steadfast love endures forever.
An inheritance for Israel his servant; his steadfast love endures forever.
Who remembered us when we were brought low; his steadfast love endures forever.

versions.text: Who remembered us in our low estate; his steadfast love endures forever.
versions.explanation: "Low estate" is archaic and can be misheard as referring to property when read aloud. A verbal clause carries the same sense with clearer rhythm for oral reading.

text: And broke us free from our foes; his steadfast love endures forever.

versions.text: And tore us free from our enemies; his steadfast love endures forever.
versions.explanation: The verb פרק pictures tearing or breaking off a yoke; "tore us free" is slightly awkward aloud, and צָרֵינוּ is more precisely "foes/oppressors" than the general "enemies."

text: Who gives food to all flesh; his steadfast love endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven; his steadfast love endures forever.
